rationale: Inbox intake whose single item is marked as the ledger's source SRC-JHONG-2026 (the founder's Substack essay, text generated by AI models at the author's direction). Under that marker its distinct testable propositions are catalogued as unfeatured, ungraded claims anchored by [p. N] and verbatim quote, and its statements bearing on existing claims enter as evidence records honest to the source's nature (an AI-written, secondary essay: context or weak supports, with limitations). Propositions already held by the ledger (VASO-C001, C002, C003, C004, C005, C010, C011, C012, C013, C020, C021, C022, C030, C031–C036) are not re-created; the essay's restatements of them enter as evidence, marked derivative where the essay only relays a primary already in the ledger. Of the 23 works the item names, one resolved to a DOI whose retrieval returned only 'Redirecting' (failed, unconfirmable); the rest were not resolved and are dispositioned as duplicates of index records, blocked with a route (where a newly catalogued claim now gives them something to bear on), or irrelevant. No source text was shown for any named work, so nothing is anchored to them. Two research items are added: the essay's PET 'metabolically cold' triple-signature prediction, which would discriminate latch from energy-crisis and inflammatory accounts, and a desk retrieval of the adverse-effects and pain–pleasure primaries behind the newly catalogued affective claims. The edition is unchanged: the new claims are hypothesis material for future editions to weigh, and nothing shown contradicts the current telling.

evidence.title: Essay restates the stress-up / relaxation-down EMG pattern at trigger points
evidence.sourceStatement: The essay states that needle-EMG studies found trigger points show spontaneous electrical chatter that rises when the "subject is given a mental stressor and falls during relaxation".
evidence.editorInference: Editor's inference: this is a secondary restatement of McNulty 1994 (VASO-E002) plus the unretrieved Banks 1998 relaxation paper; it adds no independent observation and carries zero diagnostic weight beyond E002. Same independence group as E002.
limitations: Secondary source; text generated by AI models (Kimi and Fable) per p. 1
No citation, sample size, or effect size given
Relaxation half rests on a primary (Banks 1998) the ledger has not retrieved

evidence.title: Essay's description of the latch: force persists after activation disappears
evidence.sourceStatement: The essay describes the latch-bridge state as a ratchet in which "The activating signal can disappear entirely and the grip remains." and says the founding observation is activation spiking then falling while force stays.
evidence.editorInference: Editor's inference: derivative of Hai & Murphy 1988 (VASO-E003); the phrase 'disappear entirely' overstates what the latch model claims, which is low, not zero, phosphorylation. Zero independent weight.
limitations: Overstates the model: latch is maintained force at low activation, not at none

evidence.title: The speed-of-release argument as the essay states it
evidence.sourceStatement: The essay argues that structural remodeling takes days to weeks while a knot can go in five seconds mid-exhale, so "Whatever releases in that moment must therefore be" a state rather than a structure.
evidence.editorInference: Editor's inference: this is the inference itself, not an observation; its premise (an objective seconds-scale local event) is the unmeasured thing. It supports the conditional logic of C011 only.

evidence.title: Essay asserts exhalation shifts autonomic balance parasympathetic
evidence.sourceStatement: The essay states that "Exhalation shifts autonomic balance toward the parasympathetic side" and lowers resting tone throughout the body.
evidence.editorInference: Editor's inference: uncited restatement of what Zaccaro 2018 (VASO-E009) documents; zero independent weight.

evidence.title: Essay's statement of the knot-as-latched-arteriole hypothesis
evidence.sourceStatement: The essay proposes the knot as a two-layer object: a latched arteriole upstream creating chronic local ischemia at near-zero energetic cost, producing the acidic milieu Shah found, "plus whatever skeletal fibers secondarily guard the region".
evidence.editorInference: Editor's inference: this is the hypothesis being stated by its proponent, not evidence for it; recorded for provenance of C020's wording.

evidence.title: Essay's statement of the clinging-as-latch identification
evidence.sourceStatement: The essay relays Johnson's framing that when the mind holds a prediction rigid, one "physical implementation is vascular smooth muscle latching around the relevant" tissue, and identifies this with tanha.
evidence.editorInference: Editor's inference: hypothesis statement relayed second-hand from Johnson (SRC-JOHNSON-2023 holds the primary); no evidential weight.
limitations: Second-hand relay of another author's hypothesis

evidence.title: Essay: traditional maps cluster knots along the torso midline and limbs
evidence.sourceStatement: The essay finds it "at least suggestive that the traditional maps place the important knots along the" torso's midline and the limbs, where dorsal root ganglia, sympathetic chains and dense fascia reside, rather than in the head.
evidence.editorInference: Editor's inference: an uncited assertion about the content of traditional maps, with no coding rule or chance baseline; it is the first record on C022 in either direction and carries essentially no diagnostic weight until VASO-R006 is run.
limitations: No source for the map locations cited

evidence.title: Essay asserts critics do not dispute that palpable tender spots exist
evidence.sourceStatement: After summarizing the critique (circularity, poor examiner agreement, no definitive imaging), the essay says: "what the critics do not dispute: that palpable, tender, precisely" localizable spots exist; the fight is about mechanism.
evidence.editorInference: Editor's inference: this assertion is contradicted by the ledger's critical report (VASO-E012) and by Quintner 2015 (VASO-E010), which dispute the reproducibility and status of the discrete spot itself. Recorded as the proponent's framing; it does not move C001.
limitations: Contradicted by E012/E010 already in the ledger
Uncited characterization of the critics' position

evidence.title: Essay's caveat: Mizrachi's route is vagal and skin is not parasympathetically innervated
evidence.sourceStatement: The essay notes the demonstrated route in the attention study runs through the vagal anti-inflammatory reflex over twenty minutes and that the authors note the "parasympathetic system does not innervate skin directly".
evidence.editorInference: Editor's inference: a correct limit on what C006 shows for the knot hypothesis — tens of minutes, immune route, not direct vascular grip; the ledger already reads C006 this way.
limitations: Relays the primary's own caveat second-hand; SRC-MIZRACHI-2026 is the record to cite

evidence.title: Essay: Doppler as the most consistent positive imaging result
evidence.sourceStatement: The essay states that "Doppler has quietly produced the most consistent positive results" in the imaging literature — retrograde flow, elevated pulsatility index, velocities separating active from latent points — and reads this as the latch's footprint.
evidence.editorInference: Editor's inference: consistent with Ballyns 2011 (E022) on the positives but omits the nulls the same paper reports (E024–E026); the 'latch footprint' reading is the essay's interpretation, which Ballyns's authors do not offer.
limitations: Omits the null resistivity index and 31% retrograde flow at normal sites

evidence.title: Essay restates Hubbard–Berkoff: signal vanishes a centimeter away
evidence.sourceStatement: The essay says that in Hubbard and Berkoff's recordings, if you "Move the needle roughly a centimeter into non-tender muscle" of the same trapezius the signal vanishes.
evidence.editorInference: Editor's inference: derivative of E001; the exclusivity it implies is already qualified by Simons 2002 (E031), which the essay does not mention. Zero independent weight.
limitations: Does not account for endplate-zone noise at non-tender sites

research.title: FDG-PET overlaid on elastography at palpated knots: is the stiff, electrically active spot metabolically cold?
research.summary: Small overlay study: palpate and mark knots under blinded examiners, confirm stiffness by shear-wave elastography and spontaneous activity by needle EMG at a subset, then acquire FDG-PET and compare uptake at knot sites with matched non-tender muscle. The latch account predicts uptake at or below surrounding muscle; an energy-crisis (maximally contracting fibers) or inflammatory account predicts elevated uptake. Radiation limits this to a single small study, not a census.
research.informationGain: Cold knots would be the first finding that does not fit conventional lesion taxonomies and would specifically favour a low-energy holding state over active contraction or inflammation; hot knots would fit the energy-crisis or inflammatory accounts and remove the essay's distinctive metabolic prediction. Either result moves VASO-C020 in a way no imaging of stiffness or flow can.

research.title: Retrieve the primaries behind the newly catalogued affective and adverse-effect claims (Britton; Leknes & Tracey; Moseley/Flor)
research.summary: Desk retrieval: the peer-reviewed meditation adverse-effects study from Britton's Brown program (for VASO-C133), Leknes & Tracey's review of the shared neurobiology of pain and pleasure (for VASO-C128/C130's pain-offset reading), and a primary Moseley or Flor paper on somatosensory cortical reorganization in chronic pain (for VASO-C106). Each is named only in the essay; nothing can be anchored to them until their text is read.
research.informationGain: Replaces essay-only anchors with primary sources for five claims, and tells the case whether the affective phenomenology of release (bliss, immobility, destabilization) has any instrumented literature behind it or rests wholly on testimony.
